chunks: And what Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Bint Ilyas from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a boy who breastfeeds once and twice, and he said: 'It does not make marriage forbidden.' So I counted for him until I completed ten breastfeedings. He said: 'If they are separate, then no [it does not make it forbidden].' Therefore, these two narrations do not indicate that ten breastfeedings, if they are not separate, make it forbidden except through the implication of the context (dalil al-khitab), not by their explicit text (sarih), and the implication of the context may be set aside by those who consider it sound due to the establishment of a proof for the obligation of setting it aside, and the narration that necessitates turning away from the apparent meaning of the context and also indicates it has already passed.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on separate breastfeedings making marriage forbidden in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that ten breastfeedings do not automatically establish permanent prohibition (mahramiyyah) unless they are cumulative and substantial, highlighting the juristic debate between explicit text (sarih) and contextual implication (dalil al-khitab). It underscores the Shia scholarly principle that contextual indicators can sometimes be set aside in favor of stronger evidentiary proofs, a key nuance in Usul al-Fiqh. This discussion is central to determining the validity of marriage between milk-relatives in Shia jurisprudence.
